item.title: Fleetwood-Arsenal halted for eight minutes because of drone
item.description: Referee Michael Salisbury spoke to both sides as play was halted [Getty Images] Arsenal's match against Fleetwood Town in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup was delayed for more than eight minutes after a drone was flown above the stadium while play was ongoing. Referee Michael Salisbury stopped proceedings with one minute and 40 seconds on the clock after spotting the drone flying above the pitch while Arsenal waited to take a free-kick at Highbury Stadium. The game was halted while the referee spoke to the management and staff on both benches, with police also investigating. A commentator for Sky later said police had located the drone operator. The match got back under way with 10 minutes on the clock, with Fleetwood going on to complete a famous upset on penalties . During the delay, players passed balls around as they attempted to stay warm, while supporters inside the stadium booed. After speaking to the managers and captains, the referee signalled for the players to come over to the touchline with play unable to resume. However, just as the players were about to leave the pitch, the drone flew away and play restarted shortly after. The drone then dropped to the ground in a local housing estate. Commentating on the match on BBC Radio 5 Live, Ian Dennis said: "What a shame this has happened. This is the most high-profile game in the club's history. In terms of the profile and the revenue, it's so lucrative." [Getty Images] There were seven minutes of stoppage time added on to the end of the first half because of the delay. Guidance from the Football Association on the action to be taken in such circumstances says: "Upon the sighting of a drone above a football pitch or stadium, the referee should stop the game and advise both team captains and managers that play will not continue until the drone has passed, or left the vicinity of the players and spectators." The guidance adds that if the drone does not leave, both teams should be advised to return to their changing rooms. It also recommends that, when possible, advice from the home team's safety officer can be sought. The English Football League (EFL) has had a policy on drones since the 2023/24 season which all clubs are aware of. Under the protocol, in the event of a sighting, the club's safety officer will work closely with the police, match control room and match officials to assess whether the drone presents a risk to the public or is being used with criminal intent. "As happened this evening, they work collaboratively to ensure that the drone is removed and the game restarted promptly and safely," the EFL said. item.title: Dowman sees red as Arsenal dumped out, but did Arteta go too far?
item.description: Arsenal's 16-year-old winger Max Dowman was sent off for the first time in his senior career [Getty Images] Max Dowman is used to grabbing headlines for producing moments of magic but, after being sent off in just his second start of the season as Arsenal suffered a shock loss to Fleetwood Town, the 16-year-old is facing the first test of his short career. Dowman scored twice as Arsenal beat Ipswich in the previous round of the Carabao Cup and manager Mikel Arteta rewarded him with another start in the last-16 tie at Fleetwood. And this one was perhaps more of a chance than it looked. Arsenal are currently light on options in the wing with Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis and Noni Madueke all injured. But, after being held by Fleetwood during normal time where the Gunners went behind despite having 26 shots and 78% possession, the Premier League champions lost on penalties following Dowman's red card, after a 1-1 draw in normal time. Arteta gave the youngster a scathing look as he left the pitch and angrily said something to the winger as he went down the tunnel, revealing after the game that it was "something that we discussed already before the match". The young winger reacted to a heavy challenge by Harrison Neal and, although he did not fully kick out, he made a movement towards Neal with his leg that gave referee Michael Salisbury a decision to make. It is Dowman's second red card this month after he was also sent off while representing England U19s in the last international break. "You have to remember he is 16 years of age, he's a kid," former Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson said on Sky Sports. "He wasn't having the greatest of nights so he's going to get frustrated. He gets the chance every now and then to play for Arsenal. "He probably feels he should be playing more, he gets the chance tonight, isn't doing too great. It's an old fashioned tackle. "If that's Viktor Gyokeres he [Arteta] isn't doing that. That's what I don't like. If it's an exprienced international, I don't think he does that. He's a human being. "He's not the last person to get sent off for Arsenal and he's not the first." 'It was very clear' "When we prepared the context of the match, we were very clear on the things to respect, the things that emotionally we have to dominate. It was very clear." Arteta said following the game. Dowman is one of best young players in Europe and tough treatment from defenders is something Arteta has previously said that Dowman will have to get used to. "For me, I'd put my arm round him, it's still 1-1 and you are in the game." Merson said on Sky Sports. "We all say things in life when you think 'I shouldn't have said that'. item.title: Celtics’ Jayson Tatum walks off Nets with epic OT buzzer-beater
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Celtics’ Jayson Tatum walks off Nets with epic OT buzzer-beater appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On the second night of a back-to-back, the Brooklyn Nets had the Boston Celtics on the ropes after pulling out a miraculous comeback near the end of regulation. Down by one, 124-123, the Celtics got the ball back with 2.3 seconds remaining in the contest. Everyone in the building knew where the ball was going — and Jayson Tatum still delivered. The Celtics executed their inbounds play well and forced Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. to switch on to Tatum. Tatum then took two quick dribbles to his left, pulled up for a sweet midrange shot, and swished it through the net right at the buzzer to give Boston a 125-124 victory. JAYSON TATUM CALLS GAME 🚨 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Celtics star knocks down the jumper to beat the Nets in OT! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/zbvziNHUkv — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 28, 2026 The road the Celtics took to get to this point was quite remarkable. The Nets stunned them towards the end of the fourth when Brown made the three, and Brooklyn was in control for most of the extra period. But the Nets’ inexperience showed during the final few seconds. They held a one-point lead with the shot clock off, and Brown, instead of just holding on to the ball after catching the inbounds pass, went up for a layup. This was a high-risk play, and Brown, who already missed a layup on the previous play, smoked another one, which then set up the Celtics’ opportunity to win the game. Tatum had to take on a huge workload despite being on the second night of a back-to-back, which is a sign of good health. With his game-winning shot, he finished the contest with 40 points on 10-of-20 shooting from the field (2-of-7 from deep) and 18-of-22 shooting from the charity stripe. This is a continuation of Tatum’s strong bounce-back from his horrid shooting night in the Celtics’ season-opening loss to the Detroit Pistons. Since then, the Celtics star has been averaging 33 points on 49.2% shooting from the field. With this latest victory, the Celtics have moved to 3-1 on the new campaign. Meanwhile, the Nets remain winless, and this is the most heartbreaking defeat of their season thus far. The New York Giants are sitting atop the NFC East heading into their bye week , but general manager Joe Schoen is not ready to make any bold proclamations about the team’s playoff chances. Asked how equipped the Giants are for a playoff push, Schoen kept it simple . “We’re about to find out,” Schoen said on NFL Network. “Again, I like the group. They’re resilient.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) We're about to find out." Joe Schoen on if the Giants can make a run to the playoffs 👀 pic.twitter.com/HRKujeDn97 — NFL Network (@nflnetwork) October 27, 2026 The Giants have plenty of reasons to feel good about themselves. They improved to 4-2-1 with a 27-21 overtime win over the Houston Texans on Sunday, and the victory kept them in first place in the division. J.J. McCarthy made his first start for New York in that win , and Schoen made sure to highlight what the young quarterback has done in a short time. “We have a quarterback that’s started one game for us and went out and performed at a high level. He’s 23. He’s won his last five starts,” Schoen said. McCarthy completed 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards in the win, a 71.4% completion rate that was the second-best by a Giants quarterback in his first start with the team. What impressed Schoen most was how quickly McCarthy got up to speed. The Giants acquired him from the Minnesota Vikings in late September after Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury, sending a 2027 fifth-round pick to Minnesota. “Just having played the position, how hard that is to do, to come in and the 20-plus snap counts and not really throwing to our receivers throughout a training camp or an offseason,” Schoen said. “I don’t think it’s been a month. Maybe tomorrow will be a month he’s been here. And to go out and perform against that defense the way he did was impressive.” Jameis Winston held down the fort after Dart went down, but McCarthy now appears to have taken the reins. The former No. 10 overall pick had made just 10 starts across two-plus seasons with the Vikings after an injury-riddled start to his career. He had slipped to third on Minnesota’s depth chart before the trade. Now, he has a chance to lead the Giants back to the postseason. If the Giants can build on their first-place standing after the bye, Schoen will get his answer soon enough. item.title: Reigning champ Knicks earn first win against Pistons
item.description: The New York Knicks, who broke a five-decade title drought in 2025-26 but had lost their three opening games the following season, overcame another slow start at Madison Square Garden to pull clear in the second half (Caleb Bowlin) The NBA reigning champion New York Knicks finally got their first win of the season, beating the Detroit Pistons 111-97 Tuesday with 27 points from Karl-Anthony Towns and 23 from Jalen Brunson. The Knicks, who broke a five-decade title drought in June but had lost their three opening games this season, overcame another slow start at Madison Square Garden to pull clear in the second half. They avoided the ignominy of being the first reigning champions since 1969 to start the following season 0-4. "We got to remember that Rome wasn't built in a day. This is a new year, new team," said last season's NBA Finals MVP Brunson, who added seven assists. "Adversity started early, so we just got to fight back." The Pistons -- who had won their first three games of the season -- started fast, going 13 points clear at the beginning of the second quarter thanks to free-scoring Paul Reed and Cade Cunningham. Brunson struggled early, shooting just 1-for 9 in the first half. But the Knicks pulled together for a remarkable rally, edging a single-point lead at halftime and roaring 25 points clear by the end of the third quarter. They restricted the Pistons to a combined 25 points across the entire second and third quarters. "I think we were just able to get stops, run a little bit, create a good enough lead, knowing that they were going to have a run in them to fight back," said Brunson. With a home game against Charlotte looming Wednesday, and his team 21 points down, Detroit coach J.B. Bickerstaff emptied the bench with seven-and-a-half minutes remaining. The Knicks' starters remained on court, and top-scorer Towns finished the night with 20 rebounds. The Pistons, who finished with the best regular-season record in the NBA Eastern Conference last year, are now 3-1. Reed top-scored with 22, while Cunningham had 19 points, eight assists and nine rebounds. Elsewhere, Victor Wembanyama helped the San Antonio Spurs to a 130-103 win over the Sacramento Kings with 29 points, 10 rebounds, five blocks and two steals. The Spurs, who lost to the Knicks in last season's finals, had endured their own slow start to this campaign with two opening losses, but moved to 2-2. San Antonio were rampant in a first half they led 80-54, with Wembanyama pouring in 23 points before the interval, and their lead barely dipped in a comfortable second half. Julian Champagnie scored 26 points. The Kings sank to 0-4. With Boston trailing by a single point at the very end of overtime, Jayson Tatum sank a game-winning buzzer-beater to ensure the Celtics won a thriller 125-124 against the winless Brooklyn Nets. A tense game in which neither team ever opened a double-digit lead had ended 117-117 after regular time. Tatum scored 40 points plus eight assists. amz/rcw

It told Lexington that it needed to come out with an incredibly high level of focus and take the game over right from the first whistle so they, too, wouldn’t suffer a major upset loss so early in the postseason. And they set the tone very early as sophomore Jersie Palmer scored the first goal of the night 1:06 into the game which led to an 8-0 blowout victory over Norwalk. item.title: Celtics Must Lean On White And George To Stave Off Nets Upset
item.description: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images On Tuesday night at TD Garden, the Boston Celtics welcome the Brooklyn Nets, with the stakes exceeding a mere regular season victory. Yet the Celtics face their own hurdle as they navigate the first back-to-back of the season. Derrick White is listed as probable with right hip synovitis, marking the first time he has appeared on the report this season. The team also confirmed Devin Carter is out with an illness. While Jayson Tatum, Paul George, and Mitchell Robinson are available, their minutes on Monday against the Bulls were carefully managed. George played 25 minutes and Robinson just 16. The coaching staff clearly wants to protect them, but the Nets’ poor performance might force a different hand. White’s Hip Status Defines The Rotation Derrick White has started all three games this season alongside Jordan Walsh, Tatum, George, and Robinson. His absence would force a significant shuffle in the backcourt. The term synovitis refers to swelling in the membrane that lines joints like the hip. The Colorado Center of Orthopaedic Excellence states this condition triggers inflammation that restricts movement. White played 18 minutes Monday before the issue appeared on the report. If he sits, Payton Pritchard steps in, a move that changes the defensive speed Boston relies on. Joe Mazzulla addressed the situation with a clear message about trust. He said, “We trust the sports science team that we have, we trust the competition of those guys.” However, the team has 16 back-to-backs scheduled this year. The decision on Tuesday sets a precedent for how they manage their veterans throughout the long season. Nets Desperation Makes This A Trap Game Boston cannot afford to look past a winless opponent. Visibly upset, head coach Jordi Fernandez saw the Nets suffer an embarrassing defeat against the Pacers. He stated, “The performance we put up after the first quarter was just unacceptable.” Fernandez also noted that allowing 112 points in three quarters means a team cannot win. “112 points in three quarters, you’re not winning basketball games. So it didn’t feel good on either end of the floor,” he said, according to Sports Illustrated . The Nets might think catching Boston on a back-to-back gives them an edge. Julius Randle leads the Nets in points, rebounds, and assists, presenting a physical challenge for the Celtics defense. Paul George played 25 minutes Monday and might be tired, but he is the only option to match Randle’s size. If the Celtics devolve into isolation plays, tired legs will hurt their defense. They need to run actions early to test Brooklyn’s shooting. Protecting The Lead Is The Only Goal The Celtics crushed the Chicago Bulls 134-99 on Monday, but that blowout win came with a cost. item.description: Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images Brewers’ Brice Turang makes unreal catch to throw Yandy Diaz out at first base appeared first on ClutchPoints . Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang delivered a huge defensive play in Tuesday night’s World Series Game 4, snaring a line drive and doubling Yandy Diaz off first base with the score tied 2-2. (Photo by Glenn James/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images I had a whole thing written up, but this tweet perfectly described how I felt coming into tonight’s game: A Vezina-winning goaltender will be playing for the Devils for the first time in… 4,850 days 😳 pic.twitter.com/3jAbDv6i8v — Devils Fanatics (@devilsfanatics) October 27, 2026 Since the Detroit game, the Devils have made some structural changes that have yielded a renewed focus on defense, backtracking, puck pressure, and puck support. The commitment is palpable, and we are finally getting full 60 minutes of it. Tonight was no different, and while the big storyline heading in was the debut of Hellebuyck, the real story is how we may have a wagon here boys and girls. The Devils have been overwhelmingly dominant in all 3 zones, defensively they have been reminiscent of that December shot suppression run two years ago, in the neutral zone they are a wall at the defensive blue line, and offensively they have a strong consistent forecheck and utilize hard rims to switch sides – relieving pressure and allowing for sustained possession. Transition Game One of my biggest gripes last season was the puck movement up to the forwards. Either in full-ice breakouts or short ice transitions/neutral zone regroups this team was slow and stagnant, the D would wait things out and allow opposing teams to get positionally structured and we couldn’t make anything happen. Both of Nico’s goals were perfect examples of this, the first starting with a great job by Kovacevic and Dillon to work the puck up the wall quickly out of the defensive zone, and Evangelista winning a battle at center ice, springing Nico and Timo on a 2 on 1. item.title: Runners swap streets for shopping malls as haze chokes Singapore
item.description: Fitness enthusiasts run inside a Singapore mall (Roslan RAHMAN) The pounding of running shoes echoes through a Singapore shopping mall as fitness enthusiasts desperate to exercise take refuge from choking haze. Smoke from wildfires in neighbouring Indonesia has sent air quality in the city-state plummeting to its worst levels in more than a decade in recent weeks, cancelling outdoor activities. Those seeking exercise, including runners training for international events, have found an unconventional alternative: air-conditioned shopping malls. On Sunday more than 80 runners turned the corridors of Marina Square shopping centre into makeshift running tracks, clocking laps past storefronts on two floors before shops opened for business. There are strict rules. "No sprinting, no overtaking, no shouting or yelling," Eugene Beh, 52, founder of Singapore Runners Club, told about 60 members before their run. Spitting and wiping sweat on the floor are also banned. Beh said they had to cancel several runs outdoors because of the haze, blown in by the wind from forest and peatland fires in Borneo and Sumatra. - 'Very mental' - Angeline Zeng, 57, who works in banking, completed 10 loops at the mall, or about 10 kilometres (six miles). With a half-marathon in Taipei in less than a week and a full marathon in December, Zeng needs to clock as much mileage as she can. Since treadmills at her neighbourhood gym are often full, she and her fellow runners were excited when they heard about the mall runs. "We were like, wow, we didn't expect that at all," she told AFP. "I love it because the aircon makes you feel like you're running overseas where there's cold temperatures, so it's really great," Zeng added. But she said that circling inside the mall becomes "boring" after a while. "Maybe for shorter runs this is okay but if you need to do long runs, maybe not so suitable," she said. Singapore Runners Club member Doris Tan, 42, said she thought running indoors would be a bit suffocating. "I didn't expect it to be so cool... but if you have to ask me, I still prefer outdoors," she told AFP. item.description: Joey Porter Jr. #25 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Maybe the best way to respond to incoming flak–verbal flak, that is–is often to just shrug it off, give it no attention, no oxygen and thus, no life. That’s the approach, it seems, of Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr. going back to his Week 5 illness when Dallas was playing Tampa Bay, a game that saw Porter so sick in the locker room that the team decided it was best to have him leave AT&T Stadium altogether and return home. That wasn’t easy for Porter, who had been brought in the previous week in a trade from the Steelers, after he had been unable to come to terms on a new contract with Pittsburgh. A fellow star cornerback, former All-Pro Richard Sherman, was working the game as an analyst for Amazon Prime. Sherman suggested that Porter, who was eligible to sign a new NFL contract with the Cowboys after the trade, was not really sick, but was trying to get the Cowboys to give him a new deal. Richard Sherman on Joey Porter Jr.'s illness tonight: "Maybe if they would've gave him a new contract, he would've been a little healthier today."Wow. pic.twitter.com/3zzHGfsoG7— Dom DiTommaso (@DomDiTommaso) October 9, 2026 Joey Porter Jr. Blows Off Richard Sherman On Monday night in Philadelphia, after the Cowboys won, 38-21–the first win of Porter’s Cowboys career–Fort Worth Star-Telegram beat reporter Nick Harris spoke to Porter and asked him about Sherman’s accusation that he feigned illness as a contract ploy. That talk circulated the following week. Exclusive: While the Cowboys’ locker room chaotically moved around him last night after the win, CB Joey Porter Jr. sat still at his locker staring out into the fray.For once, it was a time for him to just take in the moment.“It’s just so unreal, so surreal. I can’t even… — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) October 27, 2026 Porter Jr. did what he does best: He shut it down. “Me personally, I know the real,” he said. “I know the truth. I don’t really pay too much attention online to what they have to say. I just got to keep doing my job on Sundays. Once they see the tape, they’ll know. They’ll be quiet soon.” Cowboys Are ‘So Surreal’ After he was traded from the Steelers, the team for whom his father had played 25 years earlier, it was widely revealed that Porter had actually grown up a Cowboys fan. Fitting, then, that he might be the key piece to getting the woebegone Dallas defense turned around: Porter has allowed a miniscule 39.6 rating in his three games with the Cowboys, and did not allow a catch until a short gain by Dallas Goedert on Monday. Porter is happy to be doing this for the team he grew up watching. “It’s just so unreal, so surreal,” Porter said to Harris. “I can’t even really explain it. Sometimes it’s hard for me to be in the moment and realize what’s all going on because everything is moving so fast. I’m happy where I’m at. I’m happy where this team is headed.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Cowboys’ New Star Joey Porte

item.title: Wild Captain Jared Spurgeon Leaves Game After Blocking Two Consecutive Shots Vs Utah
item.description: Minnesota Wild captain Jared Spurgeon has not returned to Tuesday night's game against Utah after a painful sequence in the second period that saw the veteran defenseman block two shots just 15 seconds apart while shorthanded. The sequence began with 16:11 remaining in the second period when Spurgeon blocked a slap shot from Utah forward Dylan Guenther in the defensive zone. Spurgeon appeared to be injured on the initial block and was visibly struggling to move afterward. However, with the Wild still killing a penalty, the captain remained on the ice as Utah continued to apply pressure. Just 15 seconds later, with 15:56 remaining in the period, Guenther fired another slap shot toward the net. Despite already hobbling from the first block, Spurgeon managed to get in the way of the second attempt, preventing another shot from reaching the Minnesota goal. The 36-year-old defenseman then managed to clear the puck out of the defensive zone before slowly skating toward the Wild bench. Once he reached the bench, Spurgeon remained hunched over in apparent discomfort for a period of time before eventually heading down the tunnel. The extent of Spurgeon's injury remains unknown, and Minnesota has not yet provided an official update on his status. For now, the concern centers on the Wild captain, who managed to block two consecutive shots while visibly injured before finally making his way off the ice.
